holidays.name: Sidewalk Egg Frying Day
holidays.description: On the hottest day of the summer calendar, this sizzling observance invites you to crack an egg onto the pavement and see whether the sun can cook breakfast for you. Bring a spatula and a sense of optimism.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It likely grew out of the old folk challenge of testing whether a summer heat wave is hot enough to cook on concrete.
holidays.funFact: Frying an egg on a sidewalk is much harder than it looks. Concrete is a poor heat conductor and usually needs to reach well above 130°F to set an egg, and even then the egg may take a long time to cook.

holidays.name: National Caesar Salad Day
holidays.description: A day to toss crisp romaine with garlicky dressing, crunchy croutons, and shaved Parmesan. It honors one of the world's best-known salads on the same day Americans are firing up their grills.
holidays.origin: The salad is traditionally credited to restaurateur Caesar Cardini, who is said to have invented it on July 4, 1924, at his restaurant in Tijuana, Mexico. The story goes that a busy holiday weekend left him short on ingredients, so he improvised with what he had.
holidays.funFact: The salad is named after its creator, Caesar Cardini, and not after Julius Caesar. The original recipe is often said to have contained no anchovies, and the faint anchovy flavor came from Worcestershire sauce.

holidays.name: Alice in Wonderland Day
holidays.description: Tumble down the rabbit hole with a tea party, a Mad Hatter hat, and a few impossible things before breakfast. It celebrates the curious, nonsensical world of Wonderland.
holidays.origin: The day marks July 4, 1862, when mathematician Charles Dodgson, who wrote as Lewis Carroll, first told the story of Alice's adventures to Alice Liddell and her sisters during a boat trip on the River Thames.
holidays.funFact: Alice Liddell was a real child, and Dodgson later wrote the story down at her request. The published book, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, came out in 1865.
